name: Christian Light Math
line: Christian Light Math is printed lessons an adult teaches and checks. In AMP, both happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Christian Light Math: printed daily lessons an adult teaches and checks. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
verdict: Christian Light Math is a printed course of daily lessons. The adult teaches each one from a Teacher's Guide and checks the work against the answers, and review is written into the lessons [2][9]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer is checked and explained, updates the learner's level and sets the next problem.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. Christian Light places a learner in a course with a diagnostic test, and recommends beginning the test at least one grade below [7][10]. After that, quizzes and tests are built into the lessons, and the adult checks the work against the answers [5][9].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Christian Light Math the unit is the daily lesson in a printed workbook, and the adult teaches it from a Teacher's Guide [2][9]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [16].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In Christian Light Math the answers are in the Teacher's Guide or an answer key, and the adult checks the work [9]. The Answer Key Sets list answers without a full solution for every problem. Full solutions come with the textbook courses' solution keys [5]. Across 40 studies of computer feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [15].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, from counting through precalculus. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what a skill builds on. Christian Light places a learner in one course, which runs as a sequence of daily lessons [5][9][10].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Christian Light writes review into its daily lessons: many exercises return to earlier work, and the printed pages are the same for every learner [2][4][9]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks, on the researchers' own test [14].

rows.range: Grades 1 through 12: Math 1 to 8, Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2, then Functions and Trigonometry [2][8].
rows.start: A diagnostic test places the learner in a course. The publisher recommends beginning it at least one grade below [7][10].
rows.teaching: Printed daily lessons, taught by the adult from a Teacher's Guide. Algebra 1 adds optional instructor videos [9][6].
rows.next: The order of the course: the next daily lesson in the workbook [5][9].
rows.mastery: Quizzes and tests built into the lessons, checked by the adult against the answers [5][9].
rows.review: Written into the daily lessons. Many exercises return to earlier work, the same for every learner [2][4][9].
rows.print: Print is the course: workbooks, textbooks, Teacher's Guides, answer keys and flash cards [2][5].
rows.adult: Teaches each lesson from the guide, runs oral and flash-card drills in the early grades, and checks the work [2][9].
rows.reports: A paper report card for workbook scores, behavior and attendance, and a monthly progress report [7].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found. No entry in Evidence for ESSA and no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [12][13].

theirs: Christian Light Math comes from Christian Light Publications, a nonprofit publisher in Harrisonburg, Virginia, founded in 1969 [3]. It serves homeschools, Christian schools and churches [1]. The math line runs from Math 1 through Math 8, then Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2, and Functions and Trigonometry [2].

A diagnostic test places the learner in a course [10]. The learner works through consumable workbooks called LightUnits, divided into daily lessons, with quizzes and tests built in [2][5]. Each lesson brings in new ideas a little at a time, and many exercises review earlier work [9]. The adult teaches from a Teacher's Guide with detailed instructions and the answers, and checks the work [9]. The early grades add oral and flash-card drills [2].
credit: Review of earlier work is written into the daily lessons, by design [4][9].
Oral and flash-card drills build fact fluency in the early grades [2][11].
The Teacher's Guide gives the adult detailed instructions for each lesson [9].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Christian Light Math on the pages of its site we read, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][12][13].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains had the largest average effect, 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [15]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks, on the researchers' own test [14]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want to teach each math lesson yourself from printed books, with daily drills on math facts.
amp: You want each answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem, with no lesson to teach.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want printed workbooks made from your learner's own record.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Christian Light Math?
questions.answer: Christian Light Math is printed daily lessons that an adult teaches and checks against the answers [2][9]. AMP has no separate test: every answer is checked, explained and sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Christian Light Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of it on the pages of its site we read, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [12][13].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. A learner can keep the LightUnits for daily lessons and practice in AMP too. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
